verses.1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants the things which must come to pass swiftly; and He signified it, having sent through His angel to His servant John,
verses.1:2: who bore witness of the word of God and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, even of all things that he saw.
verses.1:3: Blessed is he who reads, and those who hear the words of the prophecy and keep the things written in it, for the time is near.
verses.1:4: John, to the seven churches in Asia: Grace to you and peace from Him who is, and who was, and who is coming, and from the seven Spirits before His throne,
verses.1:5: and from Jesus Christ, the faithful witness, the firstborn of the dead, and the ruler of the kings of the earth. To Him who loves us and has loosed us from our sins by His blood—
verses.1:6: and He has made us a kingdom, priests to His God and Father—to Him be the glory and the dominion to the ages of the ages. Amen.
verses.1:7: Behold, He is coming with the clouds, and every eye shall see Him, even those who pierced Him; and all the tribes of the earth shall mourn over Him. Yes, amen.
verses.1:8: "I am the Alpha and the Omega," says the Lord God, "who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty."
verses.1:9: I, John, your brother and fellow partaker in the tribulation and kingdom and steadfast endurance in Jesus, came to be on the island called Patmos on account of the word of God and the testimony of Jesus.
verses.1:10: I came to be in the Spirit on the Lord's day, and I heard behind me a loud voice as of a trumpet,
verses.1:11: saying, "What you see, write in a book and send to the seven churches: to Ephesus, and to Smyrna, and to Pergamum, and to Thyatira, and to Sardis, and to Philadelphia, and to Laodicea."
verses.1:12: And I turned to see the voice that spoke with me; and having turned, I saw seven golden lampstands,
verses.1:13: and in the midst of the lampstands One like a son of man, clothed with a robe reaching to the feet, and girded about the chest with a golden sash.
verses.1:14: Now His head and His hairs were white as white wool, as snow, and His eyes as a flame of fire,
verses.1:15: and His feet like burnished bronze, as refined in a furnace, and His voice as the sound of many waters;
verses.1:16: and having in His right hand seven stars, and out of His mouth a sharp two-edged sword going forth, and His countenance as the sun shines in its strength.
verses.1:17: And when I saw Him, I fell at His feet as dead; and He laid His right hand upon me, saying, "Do not fear; I am the First and the Last,
verses.1:18: and the Living One; and I became dead, and behold, I am alive to the ages of the ages, and I have the keys of death and of Hades.
verses.1:19: Write therefore the things which you have seen, and the things which are, and the things which are about to come to pass after these things.
verses.1:20: As for the mystery of the seven stars which you saw upon My right hand, and the seven golden lampstands: the seven stars are angels of the seven churches, and the seven lampstands are seven churches."
verses.2:1: To the angel of the church in Ephesus, write: "Thus says He who holds fast the seven stars in His right hand, He who walks in the midst of the seven golden lampstands:
verses.2:2: I know your works, your toil and your steadfast endurance, and that you cannot bear with evil men; and you tested those who call themselves apostles and are not, and found them to be false;
verses.2:3: and you have steadfast endurance, and have borne up for the sake of My name, and have not grown weary.
verses.2:4: Yet I have this against you, that you have forsaken your first love.
verses.2:5: Remember therefore from where you have fallen, and repent and perform the first works; otherwise, I am coming to you, and I will remove your lampstand from its place, unless you repent.
verses.2:6: Yet this you have, that you hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate.
verses.2:7: Let him who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will grant to eat from the tree of life, which is in the paradise of God."
verses.2:8: And to the angel of the church in Smyrna, write: "Thus says the First and the Last, who became dead and came to life:
verses.2:9: I know your tribulation and your poverty—yet you are rich—and the slander from those who declare themselves to be Jews, and are not, but are a synagogue of Satan.
verses.2:10: Do not fear any of the things that you are about to suffer. Behold, the devil is about to cast some of you into prison, that you may be tested, and you shall have tribulation for ten days. Be faithful even to death, and I will give you the crown of life.
verses.2:11: Let him who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches. He who overcomes shall by no means be harmed by the second death."
verses.2:12: And to the angel of the church in Pergamum, write: "Thus says He who holds the sharp two-edged sword:
verses.2:13: I know where you dwell, where the throne of Satan is; and you hold fast My name, and did not deny the faith in Me even in the days of Antipas, My witness, My faithful one, who was slain among you, where Satan dwells.
verses.2:14: Yet I have a few things against you, because you have there some who hold fast the teaching of Balaam, who taught Balak to cast a stumbling block before the sons of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols and to commit sexual immorality.
verses.2:15: Thus you also have some who hold fast the teaching of the Nicolaitans in like manner.
verses.2:16: Repent therefore; otherwise, I am coming to you swiftly, and I will wage war against them with the sword of My mouth.
verses.2:17: Let him who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give some of the hidden manna, and I will give him a white stone, and upon the stone a new name written, which no one knows except him who receives it."
verses.2:18: And to the angel of the church in Thyatira, write: "Thus says the Son of God, who has His eyes like a flame of fire, and His feet are like burnished bronze:
verses.2:19: I know your works, and your love and faith and service and steadfast endurance, and that your latter works are greater than the first.
verses.2:20: Yet I have this against you, that you tolerate the woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess, and she teaches and leads My servants astray to commit sexual immorality and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
verses.2:21: And I gave her time to repent, yet she is not willing to repent of her sexual immorality.
verses.2:22: Behold, I cast her onto a bed, and those who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they repent of her deeds;
verses.2:23: and her children I will slay with death; and all the churches shall know that I am He who searches minds and hearts, and I will render to each one of you according to your works.
verses.2:24: Now to you I say, the rest of you in Thyatira, as many as do not hold this teaching, who have not known the deep things of Satan, as they call them: I lay upon you no other burden;
verses.2:25: only hold fast what you have until I come.
verses.2:26: And to him who overcomes and keeps My works until the end, I will grant authority over the nations,
verses.2:27: and he shall shepherd them with a rod of iron, as the vessels of clay are shattered to pieces,
verses.2:28: just as I also have received from My Father; and I will give him the morning star.
verses.2:29: Let him who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
verses.3:1: And to the angel of the church in Sardis, write: "Thus says He who has the seven Spirits of God and the seven stars: I know your works, that you have a name that you are alive, and yet you are dead.
verses.3:2: Be watchful, and strengthen the things that remain, which were about to die, for I have not found your works complete in the sight of My God.
verses.3:3: Remember therefore how you have received and heard, and keep it, and repent. Therefore, if you do not keep watch, I will come like a thief, and you shall by no means know at what hour I will come upon you.
verses.3:4: Yet you have a few names in Sardis who have not defiled their garments, and they shall walk with Me in white, for they are worthy.
verses.3:5: He who overcomes shall thus be clothed in white garments, and I will by no means blot out his name from the book of life, and I will confess his name before My Father and before His angels.
verses.3:6: Let him who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
verses.3:7: And to the angel of the church in Philadelphia, write: "Thus says the Holy One, the True One, He who holds the key of David, He who opens and no one shall shut, and shuts and no one opens:
verses.3:8: I know your works—behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut—that you have little strength, yet you have kept My word and have not denied My name.
verses.3:9: Behold, I am giving some from the synagogue of Satan, of those who declare themselves to be Jews, and are not, but lie—behold, I will make them come and bow down before your feet, and know that I have loved you.
verses.3:10: Because you have kept the word of My steadfast endurance, I also will keep you from the hour of trial which is about to come upon the whole inhabited world, to test those who dwell upon the earth.
verses.3:11: I am coming swiftly; hold fast what you have, lest anyone take your crown.
verses.3:12: He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he shall by no means go out any longer; and I will write upon him the name of My God, and the name of the city of My God, the new Jerusalem, which descends out of heaven from My God, and My new name.
verses.3:13: Let him who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
verses.3:14: And to the angel of the church in Laodicea, write: "Thus says the Amen, the faithful and true Witness, the Beginning of the creation of God:
verses.3:15: I know your works, that you are neither cold nor hot. I wish that you were cold or hot!
verses.3:16: Thus, because you are lukewarm, and neither hot nor cold, I am about to spew you out of My mouth.
verses.3:17: Because you say, 'I am rich, and have grown wealthy, and have need of nothing,' and you do not know that you are wretched, pitiable, poor, blind, and naked,
verses.3:18: I counsel you to buy from Me gold refined by fire, that you may become rich, and white garments, that you may clothe yourself and the shame of your nakedness may not be exposed, and eyesalve to anoint your eyes, that you may see.
verses.3:19: As many as I love, I reprove and chasten; be zealous therefore, and repent.
verses.3:20: Behold, I stand at the door and knock; if anyone hears My voice and opens the door, then I will come in to him and dine with him, and he with Me.
verses.3:21: He who overcomes, I will grant him to sit with Me upon My throne, just as I also overcame and sat down with My Father upon His throne.
verses.3:22: Let him who has an ear hear what the Spirit says to the churches."
verses.4:1: After these things I looked, and behold, a door standing open in heaven; and the first voice which I had heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, said, "Come up here, and I will show you the things that must take place." After these things,
verses.4:2: immediately I was in the Spirit; and behold, a throne was set in heaven, and One seated upon the throne.
verses.4:3: And He who sat there was in appearance like a jasper stone and a sardius; and there was a rainbow around the throne, in appearance like an emerald.
verses.4:4: And around the throne were twenty-four thrones, and upon the thrones sat twenty-four elders, clothed in white garments, and upon their heads were crowns of gold.
verses.4:5: And from the throne proceed flashes of lightning, and voices, and peals of thunder; and seven torches of fire are burning before the throne, which are the seven Spirits of God;
verses.4:6: and before the throne was as it were a sea of glass, like crystal. And in the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes in front and behind:
verses.4:7: the first living creature was like a lion, and the second living creature was like a calf, and the third living creature had a face like that of a man, and the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle.
verses.4:8: And the four living creatures, each one of them having six wings, are full of eyes all around and within; and they have no rest day or night, saying, "Holy, holy, holy, Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!"
verses.4:9: And whenever the living creatures give glory and honor and thanksgiving to Him who sits upon the throne, to Him who lives forever and ever,
verses.4:10: the twenty-four elders fall down before Him who sits upon the throne, and worship Him who lives forever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying,
verses.4:11: "Worthy are You, our Lord and our God, to receive the glory and the honor and the power, for You created all things, and because of Your will they existed and were created."
verses.5:1: And I saw upon the right hand of Him who sat upon the throne a scroll written within and on the back, sealed fast with seven seals.
verses.5:2: And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice, "Who is worthy to open the scroll and to loose its seals?"
verses.5:3: And no one in heaven, nor upon the earth, nor beneath the earth, was able to open the scroll, nor to look upon it.
verses.5:4: And I wept greatly, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll, nor to look upon it.
verses.5:5: And one of the elders said to me, "Do not weep. Behold, the Lion from the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has conquered to open the scroll and its seven seals."
verses.5:6: And I saw in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a Lamb standing as though slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven Spirits of God, sent forth into all the earth.
verses.5:7: And He came and took it out of the right hand of Him who sat upon the throne.
verses.5:8: And when He had taken the scroll, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb, each holding a harp and golden bowls filled with incense, which are the prayers of the saints.
verses.5:9: And they sang a new song, saying, "Worthy are You to take the scroll and to open its seals; for You were slain, and have purchased us for God by Your blood out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation,
verses.5:10: and have made them a kingdom and priests to our God, and they shall reign upon the earth."
verses.5:11: And I looked, and I heard the voice of many angels encircling the throne and the living creatures and the elders; and their number was myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands,
verses.5:12: saying with a loud voice, "Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and might and honor and glory and blessing!"
verses.5:13: And every creature which is in heaven and upon the earth and beneath the earth and upon the sea, and all things that are in them, I heard saying, "To Him who sits upon the throne and to the Lamb be the blessing and the honor and the glory and the dominion forever and ever!"
verses.5:14: And the four living creatures said, "Amen!" And the elders fell down and worshiped.
verses.6:1: And I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying as with a voice of thunder, "Come!"
verses.6:2: And I looked, and behold, a white horse; and he who sat upon it held a bow, and a crown was given to him, and he went forth conquering and to conquer.
verses.6:3: And when He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, "Come!"
verses.6:4: And another horse, fiery red, went forth; and to him who sat upon it was granted to take peace from the earth, and that men should slay one another; and there was given to him a great sword.
verses.6:5: And when He opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying, "Come!" And I looked, and behold, a black horse; and he who sat upon it held a pair of scales in his hand.
verses.6:6: And I heard as it were a voice in the midst of the four living creatures saying, "A quart of wheat for a denarius, and three quarts of barley for a denarius; and do not harm the oil and the wine."
verses.6:7: And when He opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying, "Come!"
verses.6:8: And I looked, and behold, a pale green horse; and the name of him who sat upon it was Death, and Hades followed along with him. And authority was given to them over a fourth of the earth, to kill with sword and with famine and with pestilence, and by the wild beasts of the earth.
verses.6:9: And when He opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of those who had been slain because of the word of God and because of the testimony which they held.
verses.6:10: And they cried out with a loud voice, saying, "How long, O Sovereign Lord, holy and true, will You not judge and avenge our blood upon those who dwell upon the earth?"
verses.6:11: And a white robe was given to each one of them; and it was told to them that they should rest yet a little season, until both their fellow servants and their brethren, who were about to be slain even as they were, should be completed.
verses.6:12: And I looked when He opened the sixth seal, and a great earthquake occurred; and the sun became black as sackcloth of hair, and the whole moon became like blood;
verses.6:13: and the stars of heaven fell to the earth, even as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when shaken by a mighty wind.
verses.6:14: And the heaven parted like a scroll being rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place.
verses.6:15: And the kings of the earth, and the great men, and the commanders, and the rich, and the mighty, and every bondservant and every free man, hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains,
verses.6:16: and said to the mountains and to the rocks, "Fall upon us and hide us from the face of Him who sits upon the throne, and from the wrath of the Lamb;
verses.6:17: for the great day of Their wrath has come, and who is able to stand?"
verses.7:1: After this I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding back the four winds of the earth, so that no wind should blow upon the earth, nor upon the sea, nor against any tree.
verses.7:2: And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, holding the seal of the living God; and he cried out with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it had been granted to harm the earth and the sea,
verses.7:3: saying, "Do not harm the earth, nor the sea, nor the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God upon their foreheads."
verses.7:4: And I heard the number of those who were sealed: one hundred and forty-four thousand, sealed out of every tribe of the sons of Israel:
verses.7:5: out of the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand were sealed; out of the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand; out of the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand;
verses.7:6: out of the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand; out of the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand; out of the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand;
verses.7:7: out of the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand; out of the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand; out of the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand;
verses.7:8: out of the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand; out of the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand; out of the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand were sealed.
verses.7:9: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude, which no one was able to number, out of every nation, and of tribes and peoples and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, arrayed in white robes, with palm branches in their hands;
verses.7:10: and they cried out with a loud voice, saying, "Salvation belongs to our God who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb!"
verses.7:11: And all the angels stood encircling the throne and the elders and the four living creatures; and they fell upon their faces before the throne and worshiped God,
verses.7:12: saying, "Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom, and thanksgiving and honor and power and might, be to our God forever and ever. Amen!"
verses.7:13: And one of the elders answered, saying to me, "These who are arrayed in the white robes, who are they, and from where did they come?"
verses.7:14: And I said to him, "My lord, you know." And he said to me, "These are those who come out of the great tribulation, and they have washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.
verses.7:15: Therefore they are before the throne of God, and serve Him day and night in His temple; and He who sits upon the throne shall spread His tabernacle over them.
verses.7:16: They shall hunger no more, neither shall they thirst any more; nor shall the sun strike upon them, nor any scorching heat;
verses.7:17: for the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne shall shepherd them, and shall guide them to springs of the waters of life; and God shall wipe away every tear from their eyes."
verses.8:1: And when He opened the seventh seal, silence fell in heaven for about half an hour.
verses.8:2: And I saw the seven angels who stand in the presence of God, and seven trumpets were given to them.
verses.8:3: And another angel came and stood at the altar, holding a golden censer, and abundant incense was given to him, that he might present it with the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar before the throne.
verses.8:4: And the smoke of the incense ascended with the prayers of the saints from the angel's hand before God.
verses.8:5: Then the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and cast it upon the earth; and there came peals of thunder, voices, flashes of lightning, and an earthquake.
verses.8:6: And the seven angels who held the seven trumpets made themselves ready to sound them.
verses.8:7: And the first sounded his trumpet, and there came hail and fire, mingled with blood, and they were cast upon the earth; and a third of the earth was burned up, and a third of the trees were burned up, and all green grass was burned up.
verses.8:8: And the second angel sounded his trumpet, and something like a great mountain burning with fire was cast into the sea; and a third of the sea became blood,
verses.8:9: and a third of the creatures in the sea—those having life—died, and a third of the ships were destroyed.
verses.8:10: And the third angel sounded his trumpet, and a great star fell from heaven, blazing like a torch, and it fell upon a third of the rivers and upon the springs of waters.
verses.8:11: And the name of the star is called Wormwood. A third of the waters turned to wormwood, and many men died from the waters, because they were made bitter.
verses.8:12: And the fourth angel sounded his trumpet, and a third of the sun was struck, and a third of the moon, and a third of the stars, so that a third of them might be darkened, and the day might not shine for a third of it, and the night likewise.
verses.8:13: And I looked, and I heard an eagle flying in midheaven, saying with a loud voice, "Woe, woe, woe to those who dwell upon the earth, because of the remaining blasts of the trumpet of the three angels who are about to sound!"
verses.9:1: And the fifth angel sounded his trumpet, and I saw a star that had fallen from heaven to the earth, and to him was given the key of the pit of the abyss.
verses.9:2: And he opened the pit of the abyss, and smoke ascended out of the pit like the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the pit.
verses.9:3: And out of the smoke locusts came forth upon the earth, and power was given to them, just as the scorpions of the earth have power.
verses.9:4: And they were told not to harm the grass of the earth, nor any green thing, nor any tree, but only those men who do not have the seal of God upon their foreheads.
verses.9:5: And it was given to them that they should not kill them, but that they should be tormented for five months; and their torment was like the torment of a scorpion when it strikes a man.
verses.9:6: And in those days men shall seek death and shall by no means find it; they shall long to die, and death flees from them.
verses.9:7: Now the appearance of the locusts was like horses arrayed for battle; upon their heads were, as it were, crowns resembling gold, and their faces were like the faces of men,
verses.9:8: and they had hair like the hair of women, and their teeth were like those of lions,
verses.9:9: and they had breastplates like breastplates of iron, and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots of many horses rushing into battle;
verses.9:10: and they have tails like scorpions, and stings; and in their tails lies their power to harm men for five months.
verses.9:11: They have as king over them the angel of the abyss; his name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he has the name Apollyon.
verses.9:12: The first woe has departed; behold, two woes are yet to come after these things.
verses.9:13: And the sixth angel sounded his trumpet, and I heard a single voice from the horns of the golden altar before God,
verses.9:14: saying to the sixth angel who held the trumpet, "Release the four angels who are bound at the great river Euphrates."
verses.9:15: And the four angels who had been prepared for the hour and day and month and year were released to slay a third of mankind.
verses.9:16: And the number of the armies of horsemen was two hundred million; I heard the number of them.
verses.9:17: And thus I saw the horses in the vision and those seated upon them: they had breastplates of fiery red, hyacinth blue, and brimstone yellow; and the heads of the horses were like the heads of lions, and out of their mouths proceeded fire, smoke, and brimstone.
verses.9:18: By these three plagues a third of mankind was slain—by the fire and the smoke and the brimstone that proceeded out of their mouths.
verses.9:19: For the power of the horses is in their mouths and in their tails; for their tails are like serpents, having heads, and with them they do harm.
verses.9:20: Yet the rest of mankind, who were not slain by these plagues, did not repent of the works of their hands, so as not to worship demons and idols of gold, silver, bronze, stone, and wood, which can neither see nor hear nor walk,
verses.9:21: and they did not repent of their murders, nor of their sorceries, nor of their fornication, nor of their thefts.
verses.10:1: And I saw another mighty angel descending from heaven, clothed with a cloud, and a rainbow was upon his head; his face was like the sun, and his feet were like pillars of fire,
verses.10:2: and he held in his hand a little scroll lying open. And he set his right foot upon the sea and his left foot upon the earth,
verses.10:3: and he cried out with a loud voice, as when a lion roars. And when he cried out, the seven thunders uttered their own voices.
verses.10:4: Now when the seven thunders had spoken, I was about to write; and I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Seal up the things which the seven thunders have spoken, and do not write them."
verses.10:5: Then the angel whom I saw standing upon the sea and upon the earth lifted up his right hand toward heaven,
verses.10:6: and swore by Him who lives forever and ever, who created heaven and the things that are in it, and the earth and the things that are in it, and the sea and the things that are in it, that there shall be delay no longer;
verses.10:7: but in the days of the voice of the seventh angel, when he is about to sound his trumpet, the mystery of God shall be fulfilled, just as He declared the good tidings to His own servants the prophets.
verses.10:8: Then the voice which I had heard from heaven spoke with me again, saying, "Go, take the scroll that lies open in the hand of the angel who stands upon the sea and upon the earth."
verses.10:9: So I went over to the angel, asking him to give me the little scroll. And he said to me, "Take it and eat it up; it will make your stomach bitter, yet in your mouth it will be sweet as honey."
verses.10:10: And I took the little scroll from the hand of the angel and ate it up; and in my mouth it was sweet as honey, yet when I had eaten it, my stomach was made bitter.
verses.10:11: And they said to me, "You must prophesy again concerning peoples, nations, tongues, and many kings."
verses.11:1: And there was given to me a reed like a rod, and it was said, "Arise and measure the temple of God, and the altar, and those who worship in it.
verses.11:2: Yet leave outside the court that is beyond the temple and do not measure it, for it has been given to the Gentiles, and they shall trample the holy city for forty-two months.
verses.11:3: And I will grant to My two witnesses that they shall prophesy for one thousand two hundred sixty days, arrayed in sackcloth."
verses.11:4: These are the two olive trees and the two lampstands standing before the Lord of the earth.
verses.11:5: And if anyone desires to harm them, fire goes forth out of their mouth and devours their enemies; and if anyone should desire to harm them, in this manner he must be slain.
verses.11:6: These have authority to shut heaven, so that no rain may fall during the days of their prophecy; and they have authority over the waters to turn them into blood, and to strike the earth with every plague as often as they desire.
verses.11:7: And when they have finished their testimony, the beast that ascends out of the abyss shall wage war against them, overcome them, and slay them.
verses.11:8: And their dead body shall lie in the wide street of the great city that is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt, where their Lord also was crucified.
verses.11:9: And some from the peoples, tribes, tongues, and nations gaze upon their dead body for three and a half days, and they do not permit their dead bodies to be laid in a tomb.
verses.11:10: And those who dwell upon the earth rejoice over them and make merry, and they shall send gifts to one another, because these two prophets tormented those who dwell upon the earth.
verses.11:11: And after the three and a half days, a breath of life from God entered into them, and they stood upon their feet, and great dread fell upon those who beheld them.
verses.11:12: And they heard a loud voice from heaven saying to them, "Come up here." And they ascended into heaven in the cloud, and their enemies beheld them.
verses.11:13: And in that very hour there came a great earthquake, and a tenth of the city fell; and seven thousand persons were slain in the earthquake, and the rest were filled with terror and gave glory to the God of heaven.
verses.11:14: The second woe has passed away; behold, the third woe is coming swiftly.
verses.11:15: Then the seventh angel blew his trumpet, and loud voices sounded in heaven, saying, "The kingdom of the world has become the dominion of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever."
verses.11:16: And the twenty-four elders who sat upon their thrones before God fell upon their faces and worshiped God,
verses.11:17: saying, "We give thanks to You, O Lord God Almighty, the One who is and who was, because You have indeed taken Your great power and begun to reign.
verses.11:18: And the nations were filled with wrath, and Your wrath has come, and the time for the dead to be judged, and to grant the reward to Your servants the prophets, and to the saints, and to those who fear Your name, both small and great, and to destroy those who destroy the earth."
verses.11:19: Then the temple of God in heaven was opened, and the ark of His covenant appeared within His temple; and there were flashes of lightning, and voices, and thunders, and an earthquake, and great hail.
verses.12:1: And a great sign appeared in heaven: a woman arrayed with the sun, and the moon beneath her feet, and upon her head a crown of twelve stars;
verses.12:2: and being with child, she cries out in travail and in anguish to give birth.
verses.12:3: And another sign appeared in heaven: and behold, a great fiery-red dragon, having seven heads and ten horns, and upon his heads seven diadems.
verses.12:4: And his tail swept away a third of the stars of heaven and cast them to the earth. And the dragon stood before the woman who was about to give birth, so that when she gave birth, he might devour her child.
verses.12:5: And she brought forth a son, a male child, who is to shepherd all the nations with a rod of iron; and her child was caught up to God and to His throne.
verses.12:6: And the woman fled into the wilderness, where she has a place prepared by God, so that there she might be nourished for one thousand two hundred sixty days.
verses.12:7: And war arose in heaven: Michael and his angels fought against the dragon, and the dragon and his angels fought back,
verses.12:8: yet they did not prevail, nor was a place found for them in heaven any longer.
verses.12:9: And the great dragon was cast down, that ancient serpent who is called the Devil and Satan, the one who deceives the whole inhabited world—he was cast down to the earth, and his angels were cast down with him.
verses.12:10: Then I heard a loud voice in heaven, saying, "Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God, and the authority of His Christ, because the accuser of our brethren has been cast down, who accused them before our God day and night.
verses.12:11: And they themselves overcame him because of the blood of the Lamb and because of the word of their testimony, and they did not love their own lives even to death.
verses.12:12: Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them! Woe to the earth and the sea, for the devil has come down to you, having great fury, knowing that he has only a short time."
verses.12:13: And when the dragon saw that he had been cast down to the earth, he pursued the woman who had given birth to the male child.
verses.12:14: Yet to the woman were given two wings of the great eagle, that she might fly into the wilderness to her place, where she is nourished for a time and times and half a time, away from the presence of the serpent.
verses.12:15: And the serpent poured water like a river out of his mouth after the woman, that he might cause her to be carried away by the river.
verses.12:16: Yet the earth came to the aid of the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river that the dragon had poured out of his mouth.
verses.12:17: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went away to make war with the rest of her offspring, those who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus.
verses.12:18: And he stood upon the sand of the sea.
verses.13:1: And I saw a beast ascending out of the sea, having ten horns and seven heads, and upon its horns ten diadems, and upon its heads a name of blasphemy.
verses.13:2: And the beast that I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like those of a bear, and its mouth was like the mouth of a lion. And the dragon gave to it his power, and his throne, and great authority.
verses.13:3: And I saw one of its heads as though it had been slain to death, yet its mortal wound was healed. And the whole earth marveled and followed after the beast;
verses.13:4: and they worshiped the dragon because he had given the authority to the beast, and they worshiped the beast, saying, "Who is like the beast, and who is able to wage war against it?"
verses.13:5: And there was given to it a mouth speaking great things and blasphemies, and authority was given to it to act for forty-two months.
verses.13:6: And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme His name and His tabernacle—those who dwell in heaven.
verses.13:7: And it was permitted to wage war against the saints and to overcome them; and authority was given to it over every tribe, people, tongue, and nation.
verses.13:8: And all who dwell upon the earth shall worship it, everyone whose name has not been written in the book of life of the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world.
verses.13:9: If anyone has an ear, let him hear.
verses.13:10: If anyone is for captivity, he goes; if anyone shall slay with the sword, with the sword he must be slain. Here is the patient endurance and the faith of the saints.
verses.13:11: And I saw another beast ascending out of the earth, and it had two horns like a lamb, yet it spoke like a dragon.
verses.13:12: And it exercises all the authority of the first beast in its presence, and it causes the earth and those who dwell in it to worship the first beast, whose mortal wound was healed.
verses.13:13: And it performs great signs, so that it even causes fire to come down out of heaven to the earth in the sight of men.
verses.13:14: And it deceives those who dwell upon the earth through the signs that it was granted to perform in the presence of the beast, telling those who dwell upon the earth to make an image for the beast that has the wound of the sword and yet lived.
verses.13:15: And it was granted to it to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast might even speak and cause as many as would not worship the image of the beast to be slain.
verses.13:16: And it causes all—both the small and the great, the rich and the poor, the free and the bondservants—to be given a mark upon their right hand or upon their forehead,
verses.13:17: and so that no one may be able to buy or to sell except the one who has the mark—the name of the beast or the number of its name.
verses.13:18: Here is wisdom: let the one who has understanding reckon the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and its number is six hundred sixty-six.
verses.14:1: And I looked, and behold, the Lamb standing upon Mount Zion, and with Him one hundred and forty-four thousand, having His name and the name of His Father written upon their foreheads.
verses.14:2: And I heard a voice from heaven like the sound of many waters and like the sound of great thunder; and the voice which I heard was like that of harpists playing upon their harps.
verses.14:3: And they sing a new song before the throne and before the four living creatures and the elders; and no one was able to learn the song except the one hundred and forty-four thousand, those who had been purchased from the earth.
verses.14:4: These are those who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These are those who follow the Lamb wherever He goes. These were purchased from among mankind as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb,
verses.14:5: and in their mouth no falsehood was found, for they are blameless.
verses.14:6: And I saw another angel flying in midheaven, having an eternal gospel to proclaim to those who dwell upon the earth—to every nation and tribe and tongue and people—
verses.14:7: saying with a loud voice, "Fear God and give Him glory, because the hour of His judgment has come; and worship Him who made heaven and earth and sea and springs of waters."
verses.14:8: And another angel, a second one, followed, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great, who has made all the nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication."
verses.14:9: And another angel, a third one, followed them, saying with a loud voice, "If anyone worships the beast and his image, and receives a mark upon his forehead or upon his hand,
verses.14:10: he himself shall also drink of the wine of the wrath of God, which is poured out undiluted into the cup of His indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone in the presence of holy angels and in the presence of the Lamb.
verses.14:11: And the smoke of their torment ascends forever and ever; and they have no rest day or night, those who worship the beast and his image, and whoever receives the mark of his name."
verses.14:12: Here is the steadfast endurance of the saints, those who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.
verses.14:13: And I heard a voice from heaven saying, "Write: 'Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord from now on.'" "Yes," says the Spirit, "that they may rest from their labors, for their works follow with them."
verses.14:14: And I looked, and behold, a white cloud, and sitting upon the cloud One like a Son of Man, having upon His head a golden crown and in His hand a sharp sickle.
verses.14:15: And another angel came out of the temple, crying out with a loud voice to Him who sat upon the cloud, "Put forth Your sickle and reap, for the hour to reap has come, because the harvest of the earth is fully ripe."
verses.14:16: And He who sat upon the cloud cast His sickle upon the earth, and the earth was reaped.
verses.14:17: And another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven, he also having a sharp sickle.
verses.14:18: And another angel came out from the altar, the one who had authority over the fire, and he called out with a loud voice to the one who had the sharp sickle, saying, "Put forth your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, for its grapes are fully ripe."
verses.14:19: So the angel cast his sickle into the earth and harvested the vine of the earth, and threw it into the great winepress of the wrath of God.
verses.14:20: And the winepress was trodden outside the city, and blood came out of the winepress up to the horses' bridles, for a distance of one thousand six hundred stadia.
verses.15:1: And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvelous: seven angels having seven plagues, which are the last, for in them the wrath of God is brought to completion.
verses.15:2: And I saw something like a sea of glass mingled with fire, and those who had conquered the beast and his image and the number of his name standing upon the sea of glass, holding harps of God.
verses.15:3: And they sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, "Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God Almighty! Righteous and true are Your ways, O King of the ages!
verses.15:4: Who shall not fear, O Lord, and glorify Your name? For You alone are holy; for all the nations shall come and worship before You, because Your righteous acts have been made manifest."
verses.15:5: And after these things I looked, and the temple of the tabernacle of testimony in heaven was opened.
verses.15:6: And out of the temple came the seven angels having the seven plagues, clothed in pure, bright linen, and girded around their chests with golden sashes.
verses.15:7: Then one of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels seven golden bowls full of the wrath of God, who lives forever and ever.
verses.15:8: And the temple was filled with smoke from the glory of God and from His power, and no one was able to enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were brought to completion.
verses.16:1: And I heard a loud voice out of the temple saying to the seven angels, "Go and pour out the seven bowls of the wrath of God upon the earth."
verses.16:2: So the first went and poured out his bowl upon the earth, and a foul and malignant sore came upon the men who had the mark of the beast and those who worshiped his image.
verses.16:3: And the second poured out his bowl into the sea, and it became blood as of a dead man; and every soul of life died, everything that was in the sea.
verses.16:4: And the third poured out his bowl into the rivers and the springs of waters, and they became blood.
verses.16:5: And I heard the angel of the waters saying, "Righteous are You, the One who is and who was, the Holy One, because You have judged these things,
verses.16:6: for they shed the blood of saints and prophets, and You have given them blood to drink. They are worthy of it."
verses.16:7: And I heard the altar saying, "Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and righteous are Your judgments."
verses.16:8: And the fourth poured out his bowl upon the sun, and it was granted to it to scorch men with fire.
verses.16:9: And men were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God who has authority over these plagues; and they did not repent so as to give Him glory.
verses.16:10: And the fifth poured out his bowl upon the throne of the beast, and his kingdom became darkened; and they gnawed their tongues because of the pain,
verses.16:11: and they blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their sores, and they did not repent of their deeds.
verses.16:12: And the sixth poured out his bowl upon the great river Euphrates, and its water was dried up, that the way of the kings from the rising of the sun might be prepared.
verses.16:13: And I saw coming out of the mouth of the dragon, and out of the mouth of the beast, and out of the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs.
verses.16:14: For they are spirits of demons performing signs, which go forth to the kings of the whole inhabited world, to gather them together for the battle of the great day of God Almighty—
verses.16:15: "Behold, I am coming like a thief! Blessed is he who watches and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame."—
verses.16:16: and they gathered them together to the place that is called in Hebrew Armageddon.
verses.16:17: And the seventh poured out his bowl upon the air—and a loud voice came out of the temple from the throne, saying, "It is done!"—
verses.16:18: and there were lightnings and voices and thunderings; and there was a great earthquake, such as had never occurred since men have been upon the earth, so mighty an earthquake and so great.
verses.16:19: And the great city was divided into three parts, and the cities of the nations fell; and Babylon the great was remembered before God, to give her the cup of the wine of the fury of His wrath.
verses.16:20: And every island fled away, and mountains were not found.
verses.16:21: And great hail, about a talent in weight, came down from heaven upon men; and men blasphemed God because of the plague of the hail, because its plague is exceedingly great.
verses.17:1: And one of the seven angels who held the seven bowls came and spoke with me, saying, "Come, I will show you the judgment of the great harlot who sits upon many waters,
verses.17:2: with whom the kings of the earth committed fornication, and those who dwell upon the earth became drunk from the wine of her fornication."
verses.17:3: And he carried me away into a wilderness in the Spirit, and I saw a woman seated upon a scarlet beast, full of names of blasphemy, having seven heads and ten horns.
verses.17:4: And the woman was arrayed in purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls, holding in her hand a golden cup full of abominations and the unclean things of her fornication,
verses.17:5: and upon her forehead a name was written, a mystery: "Babylon the Great, the Mother of Harlots and of the Abominations of the Earth."
verses.17:6: And I saw the woman drunk with the blood of the saints and with the blood of the witnesses of Jesus. And when I saw her, I marveled with great astonishment.
verses.17:7: And the angel said to me, "Why did you marvel? I will tell you the mystery of the woman and of the beast that carries her, which has the seven heads and the ten horns.
verses.17:8: The beast that you saw was, and is not, and is about to ascend out of the abyss and go into destruction. And those who dwell upon the earth—whose names have not been written in the book of life from the foundation of the world—shall marvel when they behold the beast, that it was, and is not, and shall appear.
verses.17:9: Here is the mind that has wisdom: The seven heads are seven mountains upon which the woman sits; and they are seven kings:
verses.17:10: five have fallen, one is, and the other has not yet come; and when he comes, he must remain a little while.
verses.17:11: And as for the beast that was and is not, it is itself also an eighth, and is of the seven, and goes into destruction.
verses.17:12: And the ten horns that you saw are ten kings who have not yet received a kingdom, yet they receive authority as kings for one hour together with the beast.
verses.17:13: These have one mind, and they give their power and their authority to the beast.
verses.17:14: These shall make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb shall overcome them, for He is Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with Him are called, and chosen, and faithful."
verses.17:15: And he says to me, "The waters that you saw, where the harlot sits, are peoples and multitudes and nations and tongues.
verses.17:16: And the ten horns that you saw, and the beast, these shall hate the harlot, and shall make her desolate and naked, and shall eat her flesh, and shall burn her up with fire;
verses.17:17: for God has put it into their hearts to fulfill His purpose, and to be of one mind, and to give their kingdom to the beast, until the words of God shall be fulfilled.
verses.17:18: And the woman whom you saw is that great city which holds dominion over the kings of the earth."
verses.18:1: After these things I saw another angel descending from heaven, having great authority, and the earth was illumined by his glory.
verses.18:2: And he cried out with a mighty voice, saying, "Fallen, fallen is Babylon the great! And she has become a habitation of demons, and a haunt of every unclean spirit, and a haunt of every unclean and hated bird;
verses.18:3: for from the wine of the wrath of her fornication all the nations have fallen, and the kings of the earth committed fornication with her, and the merchants of the earth grew rich from the power of her luxury."
verses.18:4: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, "Come out of her, My people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues;
verses.18:5: for her sins have been heaped up even to heaven, and God has remembered her iniquities.
verses.18:6: Repay her just as she herself has repaid, and give back double according to her works; in the cup that she has mixed, mix for her a double portion.
verses.18:7: As much as she glorified herself and lived in wanton luxury, so much give to her torment and mourning; for in her heart she says, 'I sit as a queen, and I am no widow, and I shall never see mourning.'
verses.18:8: Therefore in one day her plagues shall come—death and mourning and famine—and she shall be utterly burned with fire; for mighty is the Lord God who has judged her."
verses.18:9: And the kings of the earth who committed fornication and lived in luxury with her shall weep and lament over her, when they behold the smoke of her burning,
verses.18:10: standing afar off for fear of her torment, saying, "Woe, woe, that great city, Babylon, that mighty city! For in one hour your judgment has come."
verses.18:11: And the merchants of the earth weep and mourn over her, because no one buys their cargo anymore:
verses.18:12: cargo of gold and silver, and precious stones and pearls, and fine linen and purple, and silk and scarlet, and every kind of citron wood, and every article of ivory, and every article of most precious wood, and bronze, and iron, and marble,
verses.18:13: and cinnamon and fragrant spice, and incense and ointment and frankincense, and wine and olive oil, and fine flour and wheat, and cattle and sheep, and horses and chariots, and bodies and souls of men.
verses.18:14: And the ripe fruit of your soul's desire has departed from you, and all the rich and splendid things have perished from you, and they shall never find them anymore.
verses.18:15: The merchants of these things, who grew rich from her, shall stand afar off for fear of her torment, weeping and mourning,
verses.18:16: saying, "Woe, woe, that great city, which was arrayed in fine linen and purple and scarlet, and adorned with gold and precious stones and pearls!
verses.18:17: For in one hour so great a wealth has been laid waste." And every shipmaster, and everyone who sails to any place, and sailors, and all who work the sea, stood afar off
verses.18:18: and cried out, as they beheld the smoke of her burning, saying, "What city is like the great city?"
verses.18:19: And they cast dust upon their heads and cried out, weeping and mourning, saying, "Woe, woe, that great city, in which all who had ships on the sea grew rich from her costliness! For in one hour she has been laid waste."
verses.18:20: Rejoice over her, O heaven, and you saints and apostles and prophets, for God has executed judgment for you against her!
verses.18:21: And a mighty angel took up a stone like a great millstone and cast it into the sea, saying, "Thus with violent force shall Babylon, the great city, be thrown down, and shall never be found anymore.
verses.18:22: And the sound of harpists and musicians, of flute players and trumpeters, shall never be heard in you anymore; and no craftsman of any craft shall ever be found in you anymore; and the sound of a millstone shall never be heard in you anymore;
verses.18:23: and the light of a lamp shall never shine in you anymore; and the voice of bridegroom and bride shall never be heard in you anymore; for your merchants were the great men of the earth, and by your sorcery all the nations were deceived.
verses.18:24: And in her was found the blood of prophets and of saints, and of all who have been slain upon the earth."
verses.19:1: After these things I heard what sounded like a loud voice of a great multitude in heaven, saying, "Hallelujah! Salvation and glory and power belong to our God,
verses.19:2: for true and righteous are His judgments, because He has judged the great harlot who corrupted the earth with her fornication, and He has avenged the blood of His servants at her hand."
verses.19:3: And a second time they said, "Hallelujah!" And her smoke ascends forever and ever.
verses.19:4: And the twenty-four elders and the four living creatures fell down and worshiped God who sits upon the throne, saying, "Amen! Hallelujah!"
verses.19:5: And a voice came forth from the throne, saying, "Praise our God, all you His servants, and you who fear Him, both small and great!"
verses.19:6: And I heard what sounded like the voice of a great multitude, and like the sound of many waters, and like the sound of mighty thunders, saying, "Hallelujah! For the Lord, our God, the Almighty, reigns!
verses.19:7: Let us rejoice and exult, and let us give the glory to Him, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and His bride has made herself ready;
verses.19:8: and it was granted to her to be clothed in fine linen, bright and pure." For the fine linen is the righteous deeds of the saints.
verses.19:9: And he says to me, "Write: 'Blessed are those who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb.'" And he says to me, "These are the true words of God."
verses.19:10: And I fell before his feet to worship him. And he says to me, "See that you do not do that! I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brethren who hold the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy."
verses.19:11: And I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse; and He who sat upon it is called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and makes war.
verses.19:12: His eyes are a flame of fire, and upon His head are many diadems; and He has a name written that no one knows except Himself.
verses.19:13: He is clothed in a robe dipped in blood, and His name is called The Word of God.
verses.19:14: And the armies in heaven followed Him upon white horses, clothed in fine linen, white and pure.
verses.19:15: And out of His mouth proceeds a sharp sword, that with it He may strike the nations; and He Himself shall shepherd them with an iron rod; and He Himself treads the winepress of the fury of the wrath of God the Almighty.
verses.19:16: And He has upon His robe and upon His thigh a name written: "King of Kings and Lord of Lords."
verses.19:17: And I saw an angel standing in the sun, and he cried out with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that fly in midheaven, "Come, gather together for the great supper of God,
verses.19:18: that you may eat the flesh of kings, and the flesh of commanders, and the flesh of mighty men, and the flesh of horses and of those who sit upon them, and the flesh of all men, both free and slave, both small and great."
verses.19:19: And I saw the beast, and the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to wage war against Him who sat upon the horse and against His army.
verses.19:20: And the beast was captured, and with it the false prophet who performed the signs in its presence, by which he deceived those who had received the mark of the beast and those who worshiped its image. These two were cast alive into the lake of fire that burns with brimstone.
verses.19:21: And the rest were slain with the sword of Him who sat upon the horse, the sword that proceeded out of His mouth; and all the birds were filled with their flesh.
verses.20:1: And I saw an angel descending from heaven, bearing the key of the abyss and a great chain in his hand.
verses.20:2: And he took hold of the dragon, the ancient serpent, who is the Devil and Satan, and bound him for a thousand years,
verses.20:3: and cast him into the abyss, and shut it and placed a seal over him, lest he deceive the nations any longer until the thousand years are completed; after these things he must be loosed for a short time.
verses.20:4: And I saw thrones, and they sat upon them, and judgment was given to them; and I saw the souls of those who had been beheaded for the testimony of Jesus and for the word of God, and those who had not worshiped the beast nor his image, and had not received the mark upon their forehead and upon their hand. And they came to life and reigned with Christ for a thousand years.
verses.20:5: The rest of the dead did not come to life until the thousand years were completed. This is the first resurrection.
verses.20:6: Blessed and holy is the one who has a part in the first resurrection! Over these the second death has no authority, but they shall be priests of God and of Christ, and they shall reign with Him for the thousand years.
verses.20:7: And when the thousand years are completed, Satan shall be loosed from his prison,
verses.20:8: and he shall go forth to deceive the nations that are at the four corners of the earth, Gog and Magog, to gather them for the battle, whose number is like the sand of the sea.
verses.20:9: And they went up across the breadth of the earth and encircled the camp of the saints and the beloved city. And fire came down from heaven and consumed them;
verses.20:10: and the devil who was deceiving them was cast into the lake of fire and brimstone, where both the beast and the false prophet are; and they shall be tormented day and night forever and ever.
verses.20:11: And I saw a great white throne and Him who was seated upon it, from whose countenance the earth and the heaven fled away, and no place was found for them.
verses.20:12: And I saw the dead, the great and the small, standing before the throne, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the book of life. And the dead were judged by the things written in the books, according to their works.
verses.20:13: And the sea yielded up the dead who were in it, and Death and Hades yielded up the dead who were in them; and they were judged, each one according to their works.
verses.20:14: And Death and Hades were cast into the lake of fire. This is the second death—the lake of fire.
verses.20:15: And if anyone was not found written in the book of life, he was cast into the lake of fire.
verses.21:1: And I saw a new heaven and a new earth; for the first heaven and the first earth passed away, and the sea is no more.
verses.21:2: And I saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, made ready as a bride adorned for her husband.
verses.21:3: And I heard a great voice from the throne saying, "Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and He shall dwell with them, and they shall be His peoples, and God Himself shall be with them,
verses.21:4: and shall wipe away every tear from their eyes; and death shall be no more; neither mourning nor outcry nor pain shall be any longer. The former things have passed away."
verses.21:5: And He who was seated upon the throne said, "Behold, I make all things new." And He said to me, "Write, for these words are faithful and true."
verses.21:6: And He said to me, "They have come to pass! I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End. To the one who thirsts I will give freely from the fountain of the water of life.
verses.21:7: The one who overcomes shall inherit these things, and I will be God to him, and he shall be a son to Me.
verses.21:8: But as for the cowardly, the faithless, the detestable, the murderers, the sexually immoral, the sorcerers, the idolaters, and all liars, their portion shall be in the lake burning with fire and brimstone, which is the second death."
verses.21:9: And there came one of the seven angels who held the seven bowls full of the seven last plagues, and he spoke with me, saying, "Come, I will show you the bride, the wife of the Lamb."
verses.21:10: And he bore me away in the Spirit to a mountain great and high, and showed me the holy city, Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God,
verses.21:11: having the glory of God; her radiance was like a stone most precious, like a jasper stone, crystal-clear;
verses.21:12: she had a wall great and high, and twelve gates, and at the gates twelve angels, and names inscribed upon them, which are those of the twelve tribes of the sons of Israel:
verses.21:13: on the east three gates, and on the north three gates, and on the south three gates, and on the west three gates.
verses.21:14: And the city's wall had twelve foundations, and upon them were twelve names of the twelve apostles of the Lamb.
verses.21:15: And the one who spoke with me held a golden reed as a measure, so that he might measure the city and her gates and her wall.
verses.21:16: And the city lies foursquare, and her length is as much as her breadth. And he measured the city with the reed to twelve thousand stadia; her length and her breadth and her height are equal.
verses.21:17: And he measured her wall, one hundred and forty-four cubits, the measure of a man, which is that of an angel.
verses.21:18: And the structure of her wall was jasper, and the city was pure gold, resembling pure glass.
verses.21:19: The foundations of the city's wall were adorned with every precious stone: the first foundation was jasper, the second sapphire, the third chalcedony, the fourth emerald,
verses.21:20: the fifth, sardonyx; the sixth, sardius; the seventh, chrysolite; the eighth, beryl; the ninth, topaz; the tenth, chrysoprase; the eleventh, jacinth; the twelfth, amethyst.
verses.21:21: And the twelve gates were twelve pearls, each single gate being of one pearl; and the street of the city was pure gold, like translucent glass.
verses.21:22: And I saw no temple in her, for the Lord God the Almighty is her temple, and the Lamb.
verses.21:23: And the city stands in no need of the sun nor of the moon to shine upon her, for the glory of God illumined her, and the Lamb is her lamp.
verses.21:24: And the nations shall walk by her light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory into her;
verses.21:25: and her gates shall by no means be closed by day, for there shall be no night there,
verses.21:26: and they shall bring into her the glory and the honor of the nations.
verses.21:27: And nothing unclean shall by any means enter into her, nor anyone who practices abomination and falsehood, except those written in the book of life of the Lamb.
verses.22:1: And he showed me a river of water of life, radiant as crystal, flowing forth out of the throne of God and of the Lamb
verses.22:2: in the midst of her street. And on either side of the river was the tree of life, bearing twelve fruits, yielding its fruit month by month; and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.
verses.22:3: And nothing accursed shall exist any more; and the throne of God and of the Lamb shall be in her, and His servants shall serve Him,
verses.22:4: and they shall behold His face, and His name shall be upon their foreheads.
verses.22:5: And night shall be no more, and they have no need of the light of a lamp or the light of the sun, for the Lord God shall shine upon them; and they shall reign forever and ever.
verses.22:6: And he said to me, "These words are faithful and true; and the Lord, the God of the spirits of the prophets, sent His angel to show to His servants what must shortly come to pass.
verses.22:7: And behold, I come swiftly! Blessed is the one who keeps the words of the prophecy of this book."
verses.22:8: And I, John, am the one who hears and sees these things. And when I heard and saw, I fell down to worship before the feet of the angel who was showing these things to me.
verses.22:9: And he says to me, "See that you do not do it! I am a fellow servant of yours and of your brethren the prophets, and of those who keep the words of this book. Worship God!"
verses.22:10: And he says to me, "Do not seal up the words of the prophecy of this book, for the time is at hand.
verses.22:11: Let him who acts unjustly still act unjustly, and let the filthy still be defiled, and let the righteous still practice righteousness, and let the holy still be sanctified."
verses.22:12: "Behold, I am coming swiftly, and My reward is with Me, to render to each one as his work is.
verses.22:13: I am the Alpha and the Omega, the First and the Last, the Beginning and the End.
verses.22:14: Blessed are those who wash their robes, that theirs may be the right to the tree of life, and that they may enter through the gates into the city.
verses.22:15: Outside are the dogs and the sorcerers and the sexually immoral and the murderers and the idolaters, and every one who loves and practices a lie."
verses.22:16: "I, Jesus, sent My angel to bear witness to you of these things for the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the radiant Morning Star."
verses.22:17: And the Spirit and the bride say, "Come!" And let the one who hears say, "Come!" And let him who thirsts come; let him who wills take water of life freely.
verses.22:18: I bear witness to every one who hears the words of the prophecy of this book: if anyone adds to these things, God shall add to him the plagues written in this book;
verses.22:19: and if anyone takes away from the words of the book of this prophecy, God shall take away his portion from the tree of life and out of the holy city, which are written in this book.
verses.22:20: He who bears witness to these things says, "Yes, I come swiftly." Amen! Come, Lord Jesus!
verses.22:21: The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all.

notes.1:4: The Greek places the divine title ho on kai ho en kai ho erchomenos ('He who is and who was and who is to come') in the indeclinable nominative directly after the preposition apo, treating God's eternal name as unchangeable.
notes.1:5: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads lysanti ('has loosed/freed,' supported by the earliest manuscripts), where later Greek witnesses and the Latin Vulgate read lousanti/lavit ('washed').
notes.1:6: The critical text reads basileian, hiereis ('a kingdom, priests,' echoing Exodus 19:6), rather than the later reading 'kings and priests.'
notes.1:8: Greek to Alpha kai to O names the first and last letters of the Greek alphabet (rendered 'the Alpha and the Omega'), without the later expansion 'the beginning and the ending.'
notes.1:18: Greek hadou ('Hades') denotes the realm of the dead, ordered after 'death' in the earliest manuscripts.
notes.2:13: Greek places "Antipas, My witness, My faithful one" in an abrupt nominative apposition after "in the days," and "My faith" functions as an objective genitive meaning "the faith in Me."
notes.2:22: "Onto a bed" (Greek kline) implies a bed of sickness and judgment, forming an ironic contrast with her bed of adultery; the Greek text reads "her deeds" rather than "their deeds."
notes.2:23: "With death" (Greek en thanato) reflects a Semitic idiom used in the Septuagint to denote deadly pestilence or certain mortal judgment.
notes.2:27: "Shall shepherd" (Greek poimanei) echoes the Septuagint of Psalm 2:9 and carries the dual sense of shepherding and sovereign ruling.
notes.3:5: "Thus" translates the Greek adverb houtos ("in this manner") in the critical text, rather than the variant pronoun houtos ("this one").
notes.3:10: "The word of My steadfast endurance" may denote either Christ's command to endure patiently or the word exemplified by His own patient endurance.
notes.3:14: "The Beginning of the creation of God" renders Greek arche, which carries the sense of origin, active source, or sovereign ruler of creation rather than a created being.
notes.4:1: Following the punctuation of the Greek text, "After these things" closes verse 1 to introduce the sentence continuing into verse 2, whereas many editions attach it to the end of the voice's speech ("what must take place after these things").
notes.4:3: "Sardius" denotes a deep red precious stone (carnelian), and "emerald" denotes a radiant green gem.
notes.4:11: "Existed" translates the Greek imperfect esan ("they existed") in the critical text rather than the later variant eisin ("they are"), emphasizing that all things came into being and were created through God's will.
notes.5:5: The Greek text reads simply "to open the scroll and its seven seals" without a second verb ("to loose").
notes.5:9: The Greek text reads "us" here and shifts to the third person ("them" and "they shall reign") in verse 10, a shift preserved directly from the critical text.
notes.6:6: A choenix (rendered "quart") was roughly a dry quart—about one day's ration of wheat—while a denarius was a common laborer's daily wage, indicating severe famine prices.
notes.6:8: Greek chloros denotes a pale, greenish-yellow, ashen hue; "pestilence" translates thanato (literally "death"), reflecting the Septuagint idiom for plague or pestilence (cf. Ezekiel 14:21).
notes.6:17: The Greek critical text reads "Their wrath," referring jointly to Him who sits upon the throne and the Lamb.
notes.7:5: In this enumeration of the twelve tribes, Dan is omitted while both Joseph and Manasseh appear; the Greek places "were sealed" explicitly only after Judah and Benjamin.
notes.7:14: "My lord" (Kyrie mou) is a respectful form of address to the elder rather than a divine title.
notes.7:15: "Spread His tabernacle over them" literally renders skenosei ep' autous, evoking God's sheltering presence dwelling over His people.
notes.8:7: The critical text includes "and a third of the earth was burned up," attested in the earliest manuscripts and omitted in the Textus Receptus.
notes.8:11: Wormwood (Greek Apsinthos) is a bitter plant associated in the Old Testament with divine judgment and affliction (cf. Jer. 9:15; 23:15).
notes.8:13: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "an eagle" (henos aetou), whereas some later manuscripts read "an angel" (angelou).
notes.9:11: Abaddon is Hebrew for "Destruction," and Apollyon is Greek for "Destroyer."
notes.9:13: The critical text reads "from the horns," without the word "four" found in some later manuscripts.
notes.9:16: Literally "two myriads of myriads" (twice ten thousand times ten thousand), totaling two hundred million.
notes.9:21: Greek pharmakon literally refers to drugs or potions, commonly used in antiquity for magical charms and sorceries.
notes.10:2: Greek biblaridion ("little scroll") is a diminutive of biblion (used in 10:8) and denotes a small rolled document rather than a bound book.
notes.10:6: Greek chronos ouketi estai can mean either "there shall be delay no longer" (fitting the context of 6:10-11 and 10:7) or literally "time shall be no more."
notes.10:7: The Greek verb etelesthe is an aorist passive expressing prophetic certainty ("shall be fulfilled" or "is accomplished").
notes.10:11: The critical text reads the plural "they said to me" (legousin moi), either an indefinite plural or referring to the heavenly voice and the mighty angel; later manuscripts read the singular "he said."
notes.11:1: The Greek participle "saying" appears without an explicit subject in the critical text (omitting "and the angel stood"), functioning impersonally to introduce the command.
notes.11:8: The Greek uses the collective singular "their dead body" here and in the first half of verse 9 before shifting to the plural "their dead bodies" in the second half of verse 9.
notes.11:13: Literally "seven thousand names of men," a biblical idiom denoting seven thousand individual persons (compare Acts 1:15; Revelation 3:4).
notes.11:17: The critical Greek text reads "who is and who was," omitting "and who is to come," reflecting the declaration that God's eschatological reign has now begun.
notes.12:5: Literally "a son, a male," an emphatic phrase echoing Isaiah 66:7; "shepherd" renders the Greek verb used in the Septuagint of Psalm 2:9.
notes.12:14: "A time and times and half a time" echoes Daniel 7:25 and 12:7, denoting three and a half years and corresponding to the one thousand two hundred sixty days of verse 6.
notes.12:18: The critical Greek text reads the third-person singular "he stood" (referring to the dragon), rather than the first-person "I stood" found in later manuscripts and placed at 13:1.
notes.13:1: The Greek text reads the singular "a name of blasphemy" upon the beast's heads rather than the plural "names of blasphemy."
notes.13:8: The phrase "from the foundation of the world" stands at the end of the Greek clause and may modify either "the Lamb who was slain" or "has not been written" (compare 17:8).
notes.13:10: The first clause is notably terse in Greek (literally "if anyone into captivity goes"), conveying that those appointed to captivity must endure it; the second clause uses the active future "shall slay" rather than the passive reading found in some witnesses.
notes.13:18: The number six hundred sixty-six is widely understood either as a gematria (the numerical sum of the letters of a name) or as symbolic of fallen humanity falling short of the perfection represented by seven.
notes.14:8: Greek thymos here carries the dual sense of heated passion and wrath, echoing Old Testament cup-of-wrath imagery and creating an intentional wordplay with the wine of the wrath (thymos) of God in 14:10.
notes.14:10: Literally "mixed unmixed" (kekerasmenou akratou), a vivid Greek idiom denoting wine poured into a cup at full strength without the customary dilution with water.
notes.14:19: The Greek text pairs the feminine noun lenon ("winepress") with the masculine adjective ton megan ("the great"), a characteristic grammatical anomaly in Revelation emphasizing the winepress's awesome scale.
notes.14:20: One thousand six hundred stadia is roughly 184 miles (about 296 kilometers), a symbolic number representing completeness (four squared times ten squared).
notes.15:3: Following the critical Greek text (ton aionon, "of the ages"); other manuscripts read "of the nations" (ton ethnon) or "of the saints" (ton hagion).
notes.15:4: The critical Greek text omits "You" after "fear," reading simply "Who shall not fear, O Lord."
notes.15:6: The critical Greek text reads linon ("linen"), whereas some early witnesses read lithon ("stone," either a scribal variant or an echo of Ezekiel 28:13).
notes.16:3: Greek reads "every soul of life" (pasa psyche zoes, a Semitic genitive of quality meaning "every living creature"; compare Gen 1:30 LXX), with the neuter plural phrase "the things in the sea" (ta en te thalasse) in apposition.
notes.16:5: Following the critical Greek text, which addresses God as "the One who is and who was, the Holy One" (ho hosios), omitting "who is to come" because the final judgment has now arrived.
notes.16:7: In the critical Greek text, the altar itself speaks directly, personifying the souls of the martyrs beneath it (compare 6:9), rather than introducing "another from the altar."
notes.16:16: Greek synegagen is singular, agreeing grammatically with the neuter plural "spirits" of 16:13-14 ("they gathered"), though some interpreters take God or the dragon as the implied subject.
notes.16:21: A Greek talent weighed roughly 75 to 100 pounds (about 34 to 45 kilograms), emphasizing the devastating magnitude of the final hailstorm.
notes.17:5: Greek mysterion ("a mystery") may be read either as an appositive describing the symbolic character of the name or as the opening word of the inscription itself ("Mystery, Babylon the Great...").
notes.17:8: The closing verb parestai literally means "shall be present" or "shall appear," forming an intentional parody of the divine title "who is and who was and who is to come" (1:4, 8).
notes.17:9: Greek ore ("mountains") may also be rendered "hills," a double symbol associated both with Rome's seven hills and with seven kings or kingdoms.
notes.17:16: The Greek critical text reads "and the beast" (kai to therion), showing the beast joining the ten horns against the harlot, whereas later Byzantine manuscripts read "upon the beast" (epi to therion).
notes.18:3: The Greek critical text reads peptokan ("have fallen"), whereas a well-known textual variant reads pepokan ("have drunk").
notes.18:5: The Greek critical text reads ekollethesan (literally "have been joined" or "heaped together"), whereas some manuscripts read ekolouthesan ("have followed" or "reached").
notes.18:13: The critical text includes amomon ("fragrant spice"), omitted in some later manuscripts; the closing terms somaton ("bodies," a common term for slaves) and psychas anthropon ("souls of men") highlight the trade in human lives.
notes.18:17: The Greek critical text reads ho epi topon pleon ("everyone who sails to any place," i.e., seafaring passengers), whereas later Byzantine manuscripts read "all the company in ships."
notes.19:8: Greek ta dikaiomata refers to the righteous deeds of the saints, symbolized by the bright and pure fine linen granted to the bride of the Lamb.
notes.19:10: The phrase "the spirit of prophecy" (to pneuma tes propheteias) may denote either the very essence of prophecy or the Holy Spirit who inspires prophetic witness to Jesus.
notes.19:13: The Greek critical text reads bebammenon ("dipped" or "dyed"), whereas some manuscripts read rerantismenon ("sprinkled"), echoing Isaiah 63:3.
notes.19:15: Greek poimanei ("shall shepherd") echoes the Septuagint of Psalm 2:9 in the sense of ruling with iron authority; the critical text also joins "the fury of the wrath" without a conjunction.
notes.20:5: The aorist verb translated "came to life" (mirroring v. 4) is ingressive, denoting the act of rising to life again.
notes.20:9: The critical Greek text reads simply "from heaven," whereas some later manuscripts add "from God."
notes.20:12: The critical Greek text reads "before the throne," while later manuscripts read "before God."
notes.21:3: The critical Greek text reads the plural "His peoples" (signifying the redeemed from all nations) and omits the closing phrase "and be their God" present in some manuscripts.
notes.21:6: The critical text reads the plural "They have come to pass!" referring to all the promised realities; later manuscripts read the singular "It is done!"
notes.21:16: Twelve thousand stadia is roughly fourteen hundred miles (about two thousand two hundred kilometers), giving the city the symmetrical shape of a vast cube recalling the Most Holy Place.
notes.21:24: The critical Greek text reads simply "the nations" and "their glory," without the later expansions "of those who are saved" and "and honor."
notes.22:7: Without a new introductory formula, the angel's speech shifts directly into the first-person voice of Christ, relaying His promise immediately.
notes.22:14: The earliest and best Greek manuscripts read "those who wash their robes," whereas later manuscripts read "those who do His commandments," a closely similar phrase in Greek spelling and sound.
notes.22:19: Greek manuscripts read "from the tree of life"; the reading "from the book of life" entered printed editions through back-translation from the Latin Vulgate.
notes.22:21: The earliest Greek manuscripts end concisely with "The grace of the Lord Jesus be with all," whereas later manuscripts expand the closing with "Christ," "the saints," and "Amen."
